newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW - UK Sept/Oct trade data.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - UK Sept/Oct trade data.

text.p: Following is a selection of economists' reactions to UK data showing a September global trade deficit of 899 million stg and an October non-EU trade deficit of 424 million stg:

"The figures seem much better than expected and the September global figure shows a nice positive trend in exports which will add to the positive tone in the pound. The non-EU figures are also better than expected. It is still too early to see any impact from the stronger pound but the data will dispel market fears that the rise has hit exports."
"That may not be seen until 1997. For now, the figures are an excuse to buy sterling."

"It looks as though exports are benefiting from the immediate effects of the stronger pound as export prices are rising but it has yet to feed through to demand. Ultimately it will count against exports. But the trade balance still looks good on a trend basis. That is good given we've seen the economy accelerate and import demand has stayed subdued. But that is not saying there is no danger down the road, especially if sterling continues to strengthen."
